definitions.explanation: A mistake or misunderstanding arising from incorrect perception or judgment. Often used in formal or written contexts, and most commonly encountered in the compound {試行錯誤|しこうさくご} (trial and error).

examples.japanese: {試行|しこう}{錯誤|さくご}を{繰|く}り{返|かえ}す。
{認識|にんしき}に{錯誤|さくご}があった。
examples.english: There was an error in perception.

examples.japanese: {試行|しこう}{錯誤|さくご}の{末|すえ}に、ようやく{正|ただ}しい{方法|ほうほう}を{見|み}つけた。
examples.english: After much trial and error, I finally found the right method.

notes:
Most commonly encountered in the compound {試行錯誤|しこうさくご} (trial and error), which is used far more frequently than {錯誤|さくご} alone. When used independently, it appears primarily in legal, academic, or formal written contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {試行錯誤|しこうさくご} — trial and error
- {錯誤|さくご}に{陥|おちい}る — to fall into error
- {認識|にんしき}の{錯誤|さくご} — error in perception
- {事実|じじつ}{錯誤|さくご} — mistake of fact (legal term)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {間違|まちが}い — mistake; the everyday word for errors of all kinds
- {誤|あやま}り — error, fault; slightly more formal than {間違|まちが}い but still common
- {過|あやま}ち — blunder, fault; implies a moral failing or serious mistake
- {誤解|ごかい} — misunderstanding; specifically about misinterpreting meaning or intent
